SURAH "AL-NASR" (THE HELP)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

﴿When﴾: it is in the accusative case, governed by "sabbih" (glorify), and it refers to what is yet to come. Informing of it before it occurs is among the signs of prophethood. It is narrated that it was revealed during the days of tashriq (the days of sacrifice after Eid al-Adha) at Mina, during the Farewell Pilgrimage.

﴿There has come the help of Allah and the conquest﴾: "al-nasr" (help) means assistance and victory over the enemy; "al-fath" (conquest) means the opening of lands. The meaning is: the help of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over the Arabs, or over Quraysh, and the conquest of Makkah; or it refers generally to the help of Allah given to the believers and the conquest of the lands of polytheism over them.

The verse: ﴿And you see the people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes﴾, is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to "al-nās" (the people), on the basis that "ra'ayta" means "you saw" (abṣartā) or "you knew" (ʿarafta), or else it is a second object, on the basis that it means "you knew" (ʿalimta).

﴿fī dīni Llāh afwājan﴾: this is a circumstantial clause relating to the subject of "yadkhulūn" (they enter). The answer to "idhā" (when) is "fasabbiḥ" (then glorify), meaning: when the help of Allah comes to you against those who opposed you, and He grants you the conquest of the lands, and you see the people of Yemen entering the community of Islam in great multitudes, after they used to enter it one by one, and two by two.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 110, verse 3:

﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise﴾, that is, say: "Subhan Allah" (Glory be to Allah), while praising Him; or: pray to Him. (p-690) ﴿And seek His forgiveness﴾, out of humility and as a means of abasing the self; or: persist in seeking forgiveness.

﴿Indeed, He has always been﴾, and never ceased to be,

﴿Accepting of repentance﴾. It is related that when ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) heard this, he wept and said: "Completion is a sign of decline (al-kamal dalil al-zawal)." And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lived two years after it.
